learningObjective: Reason about the memory-traffic advantage of a fused single-pass row-parallel LayerNorm.

canonicalClaims.claim: A row-parallel fused LayerNorm keeps `x` in registers/SMEM across the mean, variance, and normalize stages so `x` is loaded from HBM only once per row; a multi-pass implementation that re-reads `x` between stages would double HBM traffic for the largest tensor.
conditions: N fits in one program's tile; standard row-parallel design.
nonImplications: Does not imply Welford is unnecessary at very large N or ill-conditioned data.
Does not imply row-parallel beats sequence-parallel for all shapes.

misconceptions.claim: Two-pass mean-then-variance is numerically incorrect without Welford.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For typical FP32 shapes it is accurate enough; Welford matters at extreme N or ill-conditioned data.

misconceptions.claim: `1.0 / tl.sqrt(x)` is bit-identical across NVIDIA archs.
Triton automatically places small tensors in constant memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Triton does not manage constant memory placement automatically.

misconceptions.claim: Fusing LN doubles register pressure for no benefit.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The benefit is reduced HBM traffic; register pressure is the trade-off, not a pure loss.

implementationFacts: Row-parallel fused LN: one program per row, BLOCK ≥ N.
For long rows, use online/sequence-parallel LN to bound register footprint.
